newsitem.title: UK: CE's Northern bid in balance.
newsitem.headline: CE's Northern bid in balance.

text.p: The takevoer battle for British regional electricity company Northern Electric was set to drag into next week as predator CE Electric said Friday the deadline for acceptance of its bid was extended until Dec. 24.

CE, which is 70 percent owned by Omaha-based CalEnergy, had slapped a deadline of 1 p.m. GMT (8 a.m. EST) Friday for acceptances of its 650 pence ($10.83) a share bid which values Northern at 782 million pounds ($1.3 billion).
That deadline was extended until midnight GMT and then until Tuesday.
The company said the extension was made following a full hearing this evening of Britain's takeover panel.
"CE Electric understands that the reasons for the panel's decision will be published as soon as possible," it said.
The extension until Tuesday of the offer appeared to underline that the fate of the bid was too close to call, analysts said.
The Financial Times said it was believed CE Electric had been close to declaring victory when the takeover panel launched a late-night inquiry into issues related to the bid.
CE Electric already held nearly 30 percent of Northern, bought on the open market, and had previously declared acceptances which brought its holding up to around 34 percent.
Northern has claimed it has the backing of its largest institutional investor, the Prudential, which holds around 11 percent, as well as other funds.
The bid is the second hostile takeover that Northern has faced -- it spent 560 million pounds ($933 million) fending off Trafalgar House, now owned by Norway's Kvaerner, last year.
Northern has consistently claimed that the CE bid undervalued it and called for a higher price.
It said 700 pence ($11.66) per share was indicated in talks before CE Electric launched the offer on Oct. 28, a claim which the Americans have denied, saying that the bid was fair value.
If Northern falls to CE, it would be the 10th of the 12 cash-rich British regional electric companies set up at privatisation in 1990 to be taken over.

It would also be the fourth to be taken over by an American company with two further bids from U.S. firms Dominion Resources and Entergy for East Midlands and London Electricity, respectively, currently underway.
